name: Arcade Fire
label: Merge
lede: Arcade Fire made Funeral in a Montreal studio while relatives died, got a 9.7 from Pitchfork, sang with Bowie, took Album of the Year from Eminem, and went disco with James Murphy.

eras.title: A fire in an arcade that never happened
eras.text: Win Butler, a Texan who'd gone to Phillips Exeter, starts a band in Montreal's Mile End with his school friend Josh Deu and a McGill student named Régine Chassagne. The first lineup comes apart in public, and the one that replaces it is the band the world meets.

years.h: Two Exeter friends start a band in Montreal
years.p: Win Butler and Josh Deu recruit [[Régine Chassagne|1816f144-284b-4bca-bb70-05b1402fadeb]] at McGill, plus Brendan Reed, Dane Mills, Myles Broscoe and Tim Kile.
years.xp:
Butler says the name comes from a story someone told him as a kid, about a fire in an arcade. He later decided it was probably made up, but he believed it at the time.

That first Christmas the band recorded A Very Arcade Xmas and handed copies out as gifts.

years.h: On Mount Desert Island, one member leaves and Richard Reed Parry arrives
years.p: The band is in Maine to record its first EP. Myles Broscoe quits after tensions with Win Butler, [[Richard Reed Parry|ebb15840-19c5-4c4b-98b1-4cddeb4d7684]] joins mid-session, and Josh Deu goes back to school.

years.h: Brendan Reed quits onstage at Casa del Popolo
years.p: A show at the Montreal club ends in an argument between Win Butler and the drummer. Reed leaves on the spot, Dane Mills resigns too, and Mills tells the crowd the band has broken up.
years.xp: It hadn't, quite. Butler and Régine Chassagne kept going, and within months had new players in the rhythm section: Win's younger brother [[Will Butler|928b0e29-31d2-4c67-8377-ec93d24721b3]] and bassist [[Tim Kingsbury|a609b901-2d94-43f7-8456-8f638667a717]]. [[Howard Bilerman|39450b35-6fbc-453a-9f78-d295999617bd]], who co-owned the Hotel2Tango studio, took over the drums that summer.

years.h: Will Butler and Tim Kingsbury replace the walkouts
years.p: Win Butler's younger brother Will and bassist Tim Kingsbury join, and Hotel2Tango co-owner Howard Bilerman starts drumming for the band that summer.

years.h: The Maine recordings come out as an EP, sold at Montreal shows
years.p: The self-released Arcade Fire EP is where No Cars Go first appears. Merge reissues it in 2005, once the world is paying attention.

eras.title: Four funerals and a 9.7
eras.text: Arcade Fire made Funeral while relatives in three of the band's families were dying. It came out on Merge Records, a small label in Chapel Hill, and one Pitchfork review did a lot of the selling.

years.h: Funeral comes out on Merge, recorded for about $10,000
years.p: Mostly cut in August 2003 at Hotel2Tango, the album is named for deaths in three of the band's families inside a year.
years.xp:
The title is literal. Régine Chassagne's grandmother died in June 2003. Win and Will Butler's grandfather, the swing bandleader Alvino Rey, died in February 2004. Richard Reed Parry lost two aunts in April 2004.

Robert Christgau gave it an A-minus, calling it "too fond of drama, but aware of its small place in the big world, and usually beautiful." It was Merge's first album to enter the Billboard 200.

Wikipedia counts more than 500,000 copies sold by November 2005 and nearly 750,000 by March 2007. It went gold in the US, platinum in the UK and double platinum in Canada.

years.h: Pitchfork puts a 9.7 on Funeral
years.p: David Moore's review is widely credited with breaking the album. Pitchfork later ranked Funeral No. 2 on its list of the best albums of the 2000s.

years.h: Time's Canadian edition puts the band on its cover
years.p: That's seven months after Funeral came out on a small label in Chapel Hill.

years.h: David Bowie sings Wake Up with Arcade Fire at Fashion Rocks
years.p: An early fan, Bowie joins the band on the televised special on September 9 and appears with them several times that year. Their versions of Wake Up, Five Years and Life on Mars? go up on iTunes.
years.xp: Eight years later Bowie sang on the title track of Reflektor, which the band confirmed in September 2013.

years.h: Money starts flowing to Haiti, where Chassagne's parents are from
years.p: Régine Chassagne's parents came from Haiti. From 2005 the band sends money to Partners in Health there, and later adds a surcharge to every ticket.
years.xp: Wikipedia says the band added a dollar, pound or euro to tickets for Partners in Health and KANPE, the Haitian foundation Chassagne co-founded. The NFL licensed Wake Up for Super Bowl XLIV in 2010, and those proceeds went to Partners in Health too.

eras.title: A church in Farnham
eras.text: Arcade Fire bought a disused church outside Montreal and made Neon Bible in it, pipe organ included. The album leaked five weeks early and still went to No. 2 in America.

years.h: A disused church in Farnham becomes the band's studio
years.p: The building sits about 70 km southeast of Montreal. It's where they will make Neon Bible.

years.h: Neon Bible reaches file-sharing networks five weeks early
years.p: Peer-to-peer networks have Arcade Fire's second album by the end of January. It isn't out until March 5.

years.h: Arcade Fire make their Saturday Night Live debut
years.p: They play Intervention and Keep the Car Running. It's the first of seven SNL appearances through 2025.

years.cap: On the Neon Bible tour, July 2007
years.h: Neon Bible debuts at No. 2 on the Billboard 200
years.p: It's No. 1 in Canada and Ireland and No. 2 in the UK, for an album made in a church in Farnham.
years.xp: Intervention, with the church's pipe organ all over it, had come out on iTunes in December 2006 with the proceeds going to Partners in Health. The Neon Bible tour ran to 122 shows in 75 cities in 19 countries before ending in February 2008.

years.h: Free shows for Barack Obama in Ohio and North Carolina
years.p: Win Butler campaigns for Obama, and the band plays free concerts in Ohio in March 2008 and North Carolina in May, ahead of those states' primaries.
years.xp: In January 2009 Arcade Fire and Jay-Z were the musical guests at the Obama campaign staff ball at the D.C. Armory.

eras.title: Who is Arcade Fire?
eras.text: The Suburbs went back to the Butler brothers' Houston suburb and landed at No. 1 in four countries. Then it won Album of the Year over Eminem, Katy Perry and Lady Gaga, and a lot of viewers asked who the winners were.

years.h: The Suburbs goes home to The Woodlands, Texas
years.p: The third album looks back at Win and Will Butler's childhood in the Houston suburb. It debuts at No. 1 in the US, UK, Canada and Ireland.
years.xp:
Win Butler described it as a letter from the suburbs, neither love letter nor attack. The US first week came to 156,000 units, per Wikipedia.

The Wilderness Downtown, an interactive video made with Google and director Chris Milk for We Used to Wait, asked viewers for the address they grew up at and built the video around it.

years.h: Merge's The Suburbs takes Album of the Year at the Grammys
years.p: Arcade Fire beat Eminem, Katy Perry, Lady Gaga and Lady Antebellum, then play Ready to Start as the broadcast rolls on.
years.xp:
A Tumblr called Who Is Arcade Fire?!!! collected baffled posts from viewers who'd never heard of the band, and it became part of the story of the night.

The run kept going: Best International Album at the BRITs two days later, Album of the Year at the Junos, and the Polaris Music Prize in September.

years.h: Spike Jonze turns The Suburbs into a 30-minute film
years.p: Scenes from the Suburbs premieres at the Berlin International Film Festival and plays SXSW the next month.

eras.title: Everybody dress up
eras.text: The band went disco with James Murphy, played a secret show in disguise, and asked arena crowds to dress up. By Everything Now it had left Merge for Columbia and wrapped the record in a fake corporation.

years.h: The Farnham church goes on the market, roof collapsed
years.p: The building had been the band's studio since 2006, and the place Neon Bible was made.

years.h: A band called The Reflektors plays Salsathèque for $9
years.p: Rolling Stone prints the rule from the listing for the Montreal club show, which drew about 100 people. The band played in oversized novelty heads.
years.xp:
The listing defined formal wear as "suit, dress or something fancy." Wikipedia dates the show to September 9, 2013: $9, nine o'clock.

The heads were the ones from the Reflektor video. The show was announced at the last minute to introduce the new single and album of the same name.

years.h: Arcade Fire open SNL's 39th season, then take over NBC
years.p: NBC follows with Here Comes the Night Time, a special with cameos from Bono, Ben Stiller, Bill Hader and Zach Galifianakis.

years.h: Reflektor debuts at No. 1, with Bowie on the title track
years.p: A double album co-produced by Markus Dravs and LCD Soundsystem's [[James Murphy|6b70c46c-5c83-4cc7-99c1-e76b68919c6a]], drawing on Haitian rara.
years.xp:
It sold 140,000 copies in its first week and went to No. 1 in the US, Canada and the UK, per Wikipedia. It won the 2014 Juno for Album of the Year.

The rollout was a guerrilla campaign of cryptic logos. Win Butler said the Reflektor graffiti was inspired by Haitian veve drawings. Some of the ads damaged property, and the band apologized, saying it had meant washable chalk, not spray paint.

Kahlil Joseph's film The Reflektor Tapes followed the making of it and premiered at the 2015 Toronto International Film Festival.

years.h: Arena tickets ask fans for formal attire or a costume
years.p: The 2014 Reflektor tour wants the crowd dressed up. Critics grumble, and the band's answer amounts to relax.

years.h: Will Butler and Owen Pallett get an Oscar nomination for Her
years.p: They're nominated for Best Original Score at the 86th Academy Awards, for Spike Jonze's film, which they scored with Arcade Fire.

years.h: Everything Now arrives on Columbia, not Merge
years.p: After signing a two-album deal with Columbia in May 2017, the band sees the title track reach No. 1 on Billboard's Adult Alternative chart.
years.xp: The single was first sold as a limited 12-inch at Primavera Sound in Barcelona on May 31. In October 2017 the band parted ways with its longtime manager, Scott Rodger.

years.h: Arcade Fire post a mixed review of their own album
years.p: Everything Now Corp., the band's fictional company, runs a spoof of Stereogum's Premature Evaluation column on a site called Stereoyum, days before the album comes out.
years.xp:
The fake review predicted the real ones would be "decidedly mixed," ranked the album below Funeral and The Suburbs, and called it a bounceback after Reflektor. It said any real review would spend a paragraph on the marketing campaign: the logos, the corporate-speak, the Twitter account.

Spin treated it as satire and noted it was probably funnier if you were also a music writer. It was one stunt in a campaign that included fake Billboard headlines.

eras.title: WE, and Will goes
eras.text: Will Butler left after finishing WE, the band's second record for Columbia, and said so in March 2022. The album came out in May 2022, and Arcade Fire toured it through the rest of the year.

years.h: Will Butler tells fans he left Arcade Fire in 2021
years.p: He says he left amicably, soon after WE was finished, and announces it in March 2022. He'd been in the band since 2003.

years.h: After WE, Win Butler closes SNL with a call for abortion rights
years.p: The second Columbia album is out May 6, the day before the band plays Saturday Night Live.

q: has been mutual and always between consenting adults
years.src: Variety · The FADER · CBC · Global News · Wikipedia: Arcade Fire
years.h: Pitchfork reports sexual misconduct allegations against Win Butler
years.p: Four people accuse him of misconduct between 2015 and 2020, in a report dated August 2022. Butler says every encounter was consensual.
years.xp:
Three women, aged 18 to 23 at the time, told Pitchfork the relationships were inappropriate given the age and power gap. A fourth person, who is gender-fluid, said Butler sexually assaulted them twice in 2015. Butler acknowledged the encounters and denied the misconduct; Régine Chassagne issued her own statement backing him.

[[Feist|a670e05a-cea8-4b37-bce9-d82daf1a0fa4]] quit as opener on the European leg of the WE tour after two shows and gave her proceeds to a Dublin women's aid group; Beck later withdrew from the North American leg. CBC reported some radio stations stopped playing the band. In November a fifth woman told Pitchfork her three-year relationship with Butler, begun in 2015 when she was 22, was abusive; Butler again said it was consensual.

eras.title: Pink Elephant
eras.text: Arcade Fire came back with an app, a short tour and a record made with Daniel Lanois. Less than six months later, Win Butler and Régine Chassagne announced they were separating.

years.h: Pink Elephant arrives by way of an app called Trust
years.p: The band teases it in a mobile app, debuts songs at Luck Reunion outside Austin in March, and releases the album May 9.
years.xp:
The nine-show tour that followed ran from Mexico City on April 22 to London on May 14, with pay-what-you-can pricing at three benefit shows in New Orleans and New York. Richard Reed Parry sat it out because his wife was about to give birth.

The day after release they played SNL for the seventh time.

years.h: Win Butler and Régine Chassagne announce they are separating
years.p: They post it on Instagram. They've been married since 2003 and in the band together since 2001.

years.h: Open Your Heart or Die Trying goes ambient
years.p: Arcade Fire announce the companion record on February 4. It's a Record Store Day exclusive on April 18 and reaches streaming on May 1.
